# G10 curve inputs and market differences (fi-curve-construction)

What differs by market when you build the curve. Facts are from the cited sources; they are build hints, and the authoritative per-market convention table is [fi-g10-market-conventions](../../fi-g10-market-conventions/SKILL.md). Verify before use. Conventions change (CME discounting switched from EFFR to SOFR at COB 16-Oct-2020; the EUR/USD IBOR xccy curve was removed 6-Feb-2023).

| Ccy | RFR curve to build | OIS / futures facts | Step dates and quirks |
|---|---|---|---|
| USD | SOFR OIS, ACT/360, annual, 1M-40Y/50Y; T+2 spot; 2-day payment lag at the CCP; curve day count ACT/365F; US Government Bond calendar | SR3 ($25/bp, 39 listed, tick 0.25bp within 4 months of last trade else 0.5bp), SR1 ($41.67/bp, 13 months); index strips use the 2nd to 9th SR3; SOFR-FF basis swaps 1Y-30Y; EFFR curve = SOFR curve + EFFR/SOFR basis | FOMC effective = decision day + 1; Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec meetings often fall near the IMM Wednesday, not always on it; take dates from `cb_meetings`; SOFR is a volume-weighted median with opaque volumes, so a few bp of fixing risk remain; SRF (announced 28-Jul-2021) added a ceiling: re-estimate on post-Aug-2021 data; SOFR ≤ EFFR is not a bound. FF month-end jumps are negative. Pre-2017 SOFR OIS backfilled as FF OIS minus 4.50bp (Fleckenstein & Longstaff, Treasury Richness, 2023) |
| EUR | €STR OIS, ACT/360, annual, 1M-30Y; Euribor 3M/6M curves still live (1st-8th futures, IRS 3Y-50Y, 1s3s/3s6s/3s12s to 60Y) | LCH is the reference for EUR RFR fixings; Eurex and CME trade above LCH (CCP basis) | step on the Wednesday after the Thursday ECB meeting (effective date); month-end jumps every month, turn-of-year largest; policy path priced on €STR can differ from the policy rate; EONIA-refi spread mean 7.09bp sd 7.06bp (Oct 2005-Mar 2007); TARGET calendar; negative short forwards since 2012; tick 0.5bp |
| GBP | SONIA OIS, ACT/365F, annual, 1M-50Y; settle T+0; payment lag 0; MM year base 365 | ICE 3M SONIA futures, compounded ACT/365F, 25 listed; index strips use the 2nd to 13th | 8 MPC meetings/year, rate published 7am UK Thursday, effective that day: nodes on publication dates; nodes at MPC dates, provisional 2023, estimated 2024 (PTIRD); quarter-end premium -0.25 to -1bp the day before quarter-end (2021); one-off holidays (2023 coronation) |
| JPY | TONAR OIS, ACT/365F, 1M-40Y | | new rate effective at the start of the reserve maintenance period (16th to 15th); 1-April fiscal turn must be stripped; JGB composite spread curves for sub-sovereigns/corporates; TONA provisional and final prints are separate fixing rows |
| CHF | SARON OIS, ACT/360, 1M-30Y | SARON is secured | on 14-May-2021 the SARON forward curve was below spot beyond ~22y, SARON negative over a large range of terms |
| CAD | CORRA OIS (CDOR was discontinued after 28-Jun-2024, so the old CDOR/bankers-acceptance-futures curve is legacy history only) | CORRA futures use a 365 base | USDCAD FX settles T+1 |
| AUD | RBA cash-rate OIS (meeting-dated; one meeting per month so monthly OIS maps one-to-one); BBSW curve: IRS vs 3M 1-3Y and vs 6M 4Y-30Y; bank-bill futures 1st-8th, yield-quoted, physical delivery CTD (85-95 days) | | four partially interconnected benchmark curves, disentangling impractical: solve globally; 12M OIS-IBOR basis mean 8.82bp sd 1.46bp (2007) |
| NZD | OCR OIS; BKBM: bank-bill futures 1st-4th, yield-quoted; IRS vs 3M 2Y-15Y | | few contributors, thin markets: keep the curve hand-maintainable |
| SEK | SWESTR; STIBOR IRS vs 3M 1Y-30Y (snap 4:15pm CET since 27-Apr-2018) | | meeting-date OIS illiquid or untraded: the path is a best guess (STINA); STIBOR year-end turns were large in autumn and faded before January (fading turn) |
| NOK | NOK overnight rate; NIBOR IRS vs 6M 1Y-15Y (snap 4pm CET) | | benchmark IRS with few contributors, wide markets, periods of no trade: needs manual maintainability and inference from other markets (Darbyshire, PTIRD 2022) |

Curve snap times used by an index provider (Deutsche Bank, DBIQ Interest Rate Curve Creation Process, Feb 2023): London 4pm; NOK 4pm CET; SEK/DKK 4:15pm CET; New York 3pm; Tokyo 3pm; Sydney/Auckland 4:30pm. Never mix snaps inside one build.

## Policy-path snapshot formats (Citi, G10 What's Priced In, Aug 2026)
Table per central bank: meeting (effective date), implied rate, step (bp), cumulative bp vs the stub (OIS up to but not including the next meeting), 1-day and 1-week change. Snapshots (14-Aug-2026; stub rate / cumulative bp): FOMC 3.631%, +8.0bp at 16-Sep, +22.9 at 9-Dec, peak +36.3 at 28-Jul-27; ECB 2.188%, +23.0 at 10-Sep, +40.3 at 17-Dec; BoE 3.731%, +27.7 at 17-Dec, +57.9 Sep-27; BoC 2.277%, +78.3 Oct-27; RBA 4.347%, peak +18.3 Feb-27; RBNZ 2.500%, +105.4 Dec-27; BoJ 0.979%, +50.4 at 22-Jan-27; SNB -0.053%, +31.5 Sep-27; Norges Bank +14.0 at 24-Sep; Riksbank +25.2 at 16-Dec.
Second snapshot (fix; cumulative bp at end-26/27/28): FOMC 3.63% 25/40/37; ECB 2.19% 42/60/60; BoE 3.74% 27/57/55; BoC 2.27% 21/91/105; RBA 4.36% 15/9/4; RBNZ 2.50% 53/111/133; BoJ 0.98% 39/97/126; SNB -0.07% 4/35/49; Norges 4.26% 20/5/-25; Riksbank 1.75% 21/76/94 (Citi Markets / CitiFX Wire, What's Priced In, Aug 2026).
Footnotes to read: €STR/SONIA pricing is not the policy rate; effective vs meeting dates; JPY reserve-period timing; SEK path best guess. Probabilities and RV on the path: [stir-policy-pricing-whats-priced-in](../../stir-policy-pricing-whats-priced-in/SKILL.md).

## Data hygiene specific to curve inputs
- STIR futures close (~16:00 Chicago) vs official settle (13:59 Chicago) differ by 0.2-0.9bp: use one.
- The exchange holiday calendar differs from the federal one (closed Good Friday; open Columbus and Veterans Day): fixings and contracts follow their own calendars. A fixings series must match the curve holiday calendar exactly (a useful validator). Index-linked instruments, curves and fixings must share one index lag.
- Validate futures prices on the tick grid; flag instruments whose bid/ask is wide relative to neighbours (stale quote → oscillation); wide bid/ask observed 1W-3W 2.9bp, 1M 0.5bp, 2M 2.9bp, 3M 0.3bp, 7M-18M 3.0bp, 2Y 0.7bp in a Nov-2020 SOFR OIS set (Deriscope, Feb 2024).
- Vendor OIS replication: step forwards with continuous compounding; nodes at accrual end for ≤12M OIS and at the payment date (end + 2) for ≥18M; both legs discounted at the payment date (QuantFinance Stack Exchange, 2021).
- Day-of-week and settlement effects in the overnight rate (Thursday bill settlement up, 15th/25th up, weekends below target pre-2008) are muted under abundant reserves and may return if reserves fall (Credit Suisse, Basis Points, Feb 2010).
